latest_apis.rationale: Written natively against SvelteKit 3 (released 2026-10-01): config-in-vite, #lib subpath imports, explicit env vars, $app/state, Kit-3 goto options, the newest function-form runes compiler option, and runes/snippets everywhere — grep found no deprecated API usage at all.

app/src/routes/+page.svelte:48-56 — native form with method=get action=/ so filtering still works without JS

platform.rationale: Platform-first: fetch, URLSearchParams, modern ES (findLast, structured use of Map/Set), native form semantics as progressive enhancement, CSS custom properties and grid; no polyfills or hand-rolled substitutes.

evidence: app/package.json:8-30 — zero runtime dependencies; all devDeps are the Kit-3 toolchain (kit ^3.1.0, svelte ^5.57.2, vite ^8.3.0, vite-plugin-svelte ^7.2.0, adapter-node ^6.0.0, typescript ^6.0.3)
app/package.json:33-35 — `engines.node >=22.17` matches SvelteKit 3's documented minimum
dependencies.rationale: Every dependency is the current, Kit-3-paired major and serves a purpose; there are no runtime deps at all because fetch and the platform cover the rest. Nothing to add or remove.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/api.ts — all PokeAPI access, caching, name/type normalization and error mapping live in one module behind typed helpers (fetchApi/fetchOr404/fetchByName/cardsFor)
app/src/lib/types.ts — the server→client boundary shapes (Card, MoveRow, MoveTable, EvolutionNode) are declared once and consumed by pages
app/src/env.ts — the single place API_BASE_URL is declared, defaulted and described
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/+page.server.ts:12-22 — `Move` response interface duplicated from app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.server.ts:53-60; an API-shape change touches both

app/src/lib/server/api.ts:82 — spriteUrl derives `/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` from an ID pattern instead of the API's `front_default` field (the artwork path does use the API URL at +page.server.ts:172)
app/src/routes/+error.svelte:2-3 — reads page.error/page.status from $app/state instead of Kit 3's newer zero-config `error`/`status` props (both current; the props form is the fresher idiom)
churn_resistance.rationale: Framework or API-base changes would touch very few files thanks to the single data-access module and typed boundaries; the only ripples are one duplicated response interface and a spec-pattern-derived sprite URL.

findings.issue: The `Move` API-response interface is defined twice (also at app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.server.ts:53); a change to the API shape must be mirrored in two files.
findings.suggestion: Move the shared response interfaces (Move, Species, Pokemon) into `#lib/server/api.ts` next to TypeDetail/GenerationDetail so the API boundary is defined in exactly one module.

findings.issue: Card sprites are constructed from the documented `/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` pattern rather than the API-provided `front_default` URL, coupling card rendering to media layout assumptions.
findings.suggestion: This is a defensible optimization (avoids fetching 1025 Pokémon records for the list), but add a comment noting the pattern is spec-documented, or fall back to the API field if lists ever carry sprite URLs.

findings.issue: Uses `page` from `$app/state` to read the error/status; SvelteKit 3 also provides zero-config `error`/`status` props on `+error.svelte`, which is the newer idiom.
findings.suggestion: Consider `let { error, status } = $props()` (typed via `ErrorProps`) to match Kit 3's error-props feature; the current form is still fully supported, so this is optional polish.

findings.issue: adapter-node 6 removed the `ORIGIN` environment variable in favour of the `paths.origin` config option; the app runs behind a reverse proxy per the spec but never sets it.
findings.suggestion: No impact today — the app performs no redirects, form POSTs or absolute-URL generation — but note the `paths.origin` option for whoever first adds server-initiated navigation.

findings.issue: A failed fetch caches its rejected promise; concurrent callers within the TTL share the same rejection and render an error page instead of retrying, and failure clears only via the `.catch` cleanup.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for this workload; if resilience matters later, only cache successful resolutions and let failures retry.

summary: This app is a model SvelteKit 3 citizen, written natively in the release's idioms (config-in-vite, #lib subpath imports, explicit env vars via defineEnvVars/$app/env, $app/state, Kit-3 goto options, the March-2026 function-form runes option) with zero deprecated API usage and a lean, fully current dependency set. Data access is centralized behind one typed server module, so framework or API changes ripple very little. The only forward-looking nits are one duplicated response interface, a pattern-derived sprite URL, and an error page that could use Kit 3's newer error props.
